title: Seerah
description: General User → Beginner. Familiar facts, broader basics and short everyday lessons from the life of Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him). All questions are Beginner level; no reference-number memorization is required.
levelMethod: Beginner describes the knowledge required across all question styles. Styles are not difficulty levels. Editorial classification, not calibrated with learner response data.

review.referenceCheck: Primary-text references checked during preparation; this is not independent scholarly approval.

selectionHints.unknownResponse: Use I am not sure as a separate UI action, not a fifth option.

questions.question: Who is the prophet whose life Muslims study in Seerah?
questions.explanation: In this section, Seerah means the life and example of Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him).

questions.question: What was the name of Prophet Muhammad's father?
questions.explanation: The Prophet is identified as Muhammad ibn Abdullah in the Hudaybiyyah account.

questions.question: To which tribe did the Prophet belong?
questions.explanation: The Prophet belonged to Quraysh.

questions.question: Which clan of Quraysh did the Prophet belong to?
questions.explanation: The Prophet was from Banu Hashim within Quraysh.

questions.question: What childhood circumstance does the Quran recall about the Prophet?

options.text: He grew up as a king.
He commanded an army as a child.

questions.explanation: Surah Ad-Duha recalls Allah giving shelter to the Prophet as an orphan.

questions.question: In which cave did the first Quranic revelation come?
questions.explanation: The first-revelation account names the cave of Hira.

questions.question: Which wife comforted the Prophet after the first revelation?
questions.explanation: Khadijah reassured him after the experience of revelation.

questions.question: Which angel brought the Quran to the Prophet?
questions.explanation: Jibril brought the Quran by Allah's permission.

questions.question: About how old was the Prophet when revelation began?
questions.explanation: Anas's description places the beginning of revelation at forty.

questions.question: The first Quranic revelation included the opening of which surah?
questions.explanation: The first-revelation narration includes the opening verses of Al-Alaq.

questions.question: From which city did the Prophet leave for the Hijrah to Madinah?
questions.explanation: The migration account describes the departure from Makkah.

questions.question: To which city did the Prophet migrate?
questions.explanation: Madinah was the destination of the Hijrah.

questions.question: Who accompanied the Prophet during the Hijrah?
questions.explanation: Abu Bakr accompanied the Prophet on the migration journey.

questions.question: In which cave did the Prophet and Abu Bakr stay during the Hijrah?
questions.explanation: They stayed in a cave on Mount Thawr during the migration.

questions.question: In which city did the Prophet help establish his mosque after the Hijrah?
questions.explanation: The arrival account describes the building of the mosque in Madinah.

questions.question: Which of these was a daughter of the Prophet?
questions.explanation: Fatimah is identified as the Prophet's daughter in the account of his final illness.

questions.question: Which grandson did the Prophet kiss in a well-known narration about mercy?
questions.explanation: The narration describes the Prophet kissing Al-Hasan ibn Ali.

questions.question: Which son of the Prophet died as a young child in the narration about his tears?
questions.explanation: The narration records the Prophet's grief at the death of his son Ibrahim.

questions.question: Which companion described serving the Prophet for ten years?
questions.explanation: Anas described the Prophet's patient treatment during his years of service.

questions.question: What does Islam teach about Muhammad's place among the prophets?

options.text: He is a partner in worship.

questions.explanation: The Quran identifies Muhammad as Allah's Messenger and the seal of the prophets.

questions.question: What did Khadijah recall when reassuring the Prophet?

options.text: His kindness and help for people
His wish to avoid every responsibility

questions.explanation: She recalled qualities such as family care, hospitality and helping those in difficulty.

questions.question: Whom did Khadijah take the Prophet to after the first revelation?
questions.explanation: Khadijah consulted Waraqah, who knew earlier scripture.

questions.question: From which place did the Prophet call Quraysh to give a public warning?
questions.explanation: The account describes him calling the clans of Quraysh from Al-Safa.

questions.question: At Al-Safa, what did the people acknowledge about the Prophet's speech?

options.text: They had known him to speak truthfully.

questions.explanation: Before the warning, the listeners acknowledged his truthfulness.

questions.question: Who helped prepare food for the Prophet and Abu Bakr's migration?
questions.explanation: The migration account describes Asma helping with the journey's provisions.

questions.question: Who were the Ansar?
questions.explanation: The Ansar were the Madinan supporters who welcomed and helped the emigrants.

questions.question: What does Muhajirun refer to in the early Muslim community?

options.text: The keepers of a royal palace

questions.explanation: The Quran names the Muhajirun, or emigrants, alongside the Ansar.

questions.question: Which companion hosted the Prophet on his arrival in Madinah?
questions.explanation: The arrival narration places the Prophet at Abu Ayyub's home.

questions.question: Did the Prophet join the community in work during the building of the mosque?
questions.explanation: The arrival account places him with the companions during the building work.

questions.question: Which battle is named in the Quran as an occasion of Allah's help to the early Muslims?
questions.explanation: The Quran explicitly names Badr when recalling Allah's help.

questions.question: What was Hudaybiyyah especially known for?
questions.explanation: The Hudaybiyyah account describes negotiations and a peace agreement.

questions.question: At the conquest of Makkah, what did the Prophet remove from around the Kabah?
questions.explanation: The narration describes the removal of idols around the Kabah.

questions.question: What is the Prophet's final Hajj commonly called?
questions.explanation: The Prophet's Hajj near the end of his life is known as the Farewell Pilgrimage.

questions.question: How did Aishah describe the Prophet's conduct at home?
questions.explanation: Aishah described him serving his family and going out for prayer.

questions.question: What did the Prophet's affection toward his grandson demonstrate?

options.text: That children should never be greeted

questions.explanation: The account connects affection toward a child with mercy.

questions.question: What did Anas remember about the Prophet's treatment of him?

options.text: He demanded gifts for every lesson.
He refused to speak to him at all.
He did not speak to him with impatient contempt.

questions.explanation: Anas recalled remarkable patience and the absence of harsh reproach.

questions.question: According to Ibn Abbas, when was the Prophet especially generous?
questions.explanation: Ibn Abbas described his increased generosity in Ramadan.

questions.question: When choosing between two options, what did the Prophet prefer if neither involved sin?

options.text: The more painful option simply because it hurt
The option that gained more applause
The option that caused more confusion

questions.explanation: Aishah described his preference for ease when the choice was not sinful.

questions.question: Did the Prophet shed tears when his son Ibrahim died?

options.text: No, he said all tears were forbidden.
Only because someone ordered him to

questions.explanation: His tears expressed mercy and grief while his speech remained pleasing to Allah.

questions.question: How does the Quran describe the Prophet's mission in relation to the worlds?

options.text: As a pursuit of wealth alone
As a reason to reject all learning

questions.explanation: The Quran describes him as sent as a mercy to the worlds.

questions.question: Your family needs help with chores. Which choice follows the Prophet's example?

options.text: Refuse because helping lowers your status.
Leave every task for someone else.

questions.explanation: The Prophet served his family at home.

questions.question: A young child wants your attention. Which response reflects the Prophet's tenderness?
questions.explanation: The Prophet's affection toward children teaches mercy.

questions.question: Someone helping you makes a mistake. What reflects the patience Anas remembered?

options.text: Mock them in front of others.
Treat the mistake as a reason for cruelty.

questions.explanation: Anas's account highlights patient treatment rather than harsh reproach.

questions.question: Telling the truth may be uncomfortable. What follows the Prophet's truthful example?

options.text: Invent a story to look better.
Let popularity decide what is true.

questions.explanation: His public reputation for truthfulness is recalled in the Al-Safa account.

questions.question: You are preparing for an important journey. What lesson fits the Hijrah account?

options.text: Avoid all planning to prove faith.
Assume trust means ignoring every practical need.
Rely on a lucky number instead of preparation.

questions.explanation: The migration included provisions, transport and a guide.

questions.question: A newcomer needs support in your community. Which example can inspire you?

options.text: Mocking people who arrive with little

questions.explanation: The Quran praises the receiving community's care for the emigrants.

questions.question: Your community is doing useful shared work. What reflects the Prophet's example during mosque construction?

options.text: Join in as you are able.

questions.explanation: The mosque-building account shows participation alongside the community.

questions.question: A loved one is frightened after a difficult experience. What can you learn from Khadijah?

options.text: Demand they never speak about it.
Humiliate them in front of others.

questions.explanation: Khadijah responded to the Prophet's distress with comfort and reassurance.

questions.question: You want to follow the Prophet's example in Ramadan. Which quality should you practise?

options.text: Keeping every useful thing from others

questions.explanation: The Prophet was especially generous during Ramadan.

questions.question: Two lawful ways to complete a task are available. Is choosing the easier one necessarily wrong?

options.text: Yes, hardship is always the only goal.
Yes, every easier option is forbidden.

questions.explanation: The Prophet chose the easier option when it did not involve sin.

questions.question: You are grieving a loss. Does the Prophet's example show that tears can go with faith?

options.text: Only if no one sees you

questions.explanation: He wept at Ibrahim's death and still spoke with faith and restraint.

questions.question: An old family friend needs kindness. Which example can guide you?

options.text: Helping only people who can repay you
Ignoring someone because they are not famous

questions.explanation: Aishah recalled the Prophet sending gifts to Khadijah's friends.

questions.question: You are explaining something useful. Which habit reflects Aishah's description of the Prophet's speech?

options.text: Speak clearly so listeners can understand.
Rush so no one can follow.

questions.explanation: Aishah described speech that listeners could follow, rather than hurried speech.

questions.question: You meet a group of children. Which action follows a reported practice of the Prophet?

options.text: Ignore them because of their age.
Say greetings are only for adults.

questions.explanation: Anas recalled the Prophet greeting children.

questions.question: A beginner asks how to pray. Which response fits the Prophet's teaching example?

options.text: Tell them questions have no place.

questions.explanation: The Prophet explained the prayer to a man who needed correction.

questions.question: You need a practical solution and a trusted person offers useful advice. Which Seerah example supports listening?

options.text: Rejecting advice solely because it came from family
Assuming leadership means knowing every practical answer alone
The Prophet listening to Umm Salamah at Hudaybiyyah

questions.explanation: The Hudaybiyyah narration records Umm Salamah's helpful advice and the Prophet acting on it.

questions.question: Someone disagrees with you. Which quality fits the Prophet's merciful leadership?
questions.explanation: The Quran describes the Prophet's gentleness and warns that harshness would drive people away.

questions.question: You want your household to benefit from Ramadan's final nights. Which example can guide you?

options.text: The Prophet encouraging his family to worship
Making worship only about public praise

questions.explanation: Aishah described him waking his family during the last ten nights.

questions.question: People reject your good advice. Which response reflects the hope in the Prophet's account after rejection near Taif?

options.text: Assume no one from that community can ever change.
Treat rejection as permission for every cruelty.
Keep concern for people's guidance instead of wishing destruction on everyone.
Invent false claims to punish them.

questions.explanation: The Prophet declined the offered destruction and hoped for descendants who would worship Allah.

questions.question: You learn a story from the Prophet's life. What is a useful next step?

options.text: Invent extra dialogue and call it revelation.
Assume remembering a name is the only purpose.
Treat his example as unrelated to daily life.
Look for a sound lesson to practise.

questions.explanation: The Quran presents the Messenger as an example for believers.
